purpose: Individual reconciliation against each existing scope. Completed review is not product certification or proof that every gap is resolved.

applications.name: Shotcut
E3: The XML checker resolves and rewrites missing resource paths, and changed hashes reset selected stream/metadata state. No complete timeline/media/filter/proxy packet has been independently reconstructed with equivalent interpretation or rendering. Relinking source logic alone does not establish project survival.
E5: Autosave lookup and removal identify transient recovery files, not durable version history. Effective save/overwrite, media relink, filter/script authority and usable correction after failed edits or autosave cleanup remain insufficiently covered.
longevity: E3 is not established for Shotcut's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.
applications.remaining: A complex timeline reopened/rendered independently, filter/proxy closure, actual crash recovery, older-version opening and media consolidation remain untested. E5 needs save/relink/overwrite and filter/script controls, inspectable changes and actual transient-autosave correction boundaries.
applications.current_remaining: A complex timeline reopened/rendered independently, filter/proxy closure, actual crash recovery, older-version opening and media consolidation remain untested. E5 needs save/relink/overwrite and filter/script controls, inspectable changes and actual transient-autosave correction boundaries.
applications.next: Inspect a synthetic full project/media/proxy/filter packet with expected timeline and reference output; obtain same-version relink/save/autosave recovery records from upstream or another assessor.
sovereignty: A positive Sovereignty finding requires established E1, E2 and E4 in the declared scope. The existing access/exit/custody record for Shotcut does not establish all three minimums. The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.

applications.name: REAPER
E3: The SDK exposes textual project-state/import interfaces but does not fully specify proprietary-core or arbitrary plugin chunks. Complete RPP/media/plugin/automation reconstruction and compatible offline continuation have not been independently demonstrated.
E5: SDK save/load and undo context flags explicitly allow extensions to choose saved undo state. Those contracts are not full evidence of effective script/plugin authority, destructive media operations, consolidation/output overwrite and correction in the assessed core/configuration.
longevity: E3 is not established for REAPER's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.
applications.remaining: Actual RPP/plugin-state inspection, backup/autosave defaults, clean-host consolidation, stem equivalence, version compatibility and evaluation-license behavior remain untested; the proprietary core was not inspected. E5 needs core/configuration-specific plugin/script and media/save/export control, with explicit extension undo and backup limits.
applications.current_remaining: Actual RPP/plugin-state inspection, backup/autosave defaults, clean-host consolidation, stem equivalence, version compatibility and evaluation-license behavior remain untested; the proprietary core was not inspected. E5 needs core/configuration-specific plugin/script and media/save/export control, with explicit extension undo and backup limits.
applications.next: Inspect a synthetic RPP/media/extension-state packet and dependency manifest with expected routing/automation/stems; obtain robust same-version independent save/undo/consolidation observations since the proprietary core is not available for source inspection.
E2: The former E2 Pass does not establish a replacement editable audio workflow preserving routing, automation and plugin-dependent meaning. Consolidated media and rendered stems are useful handoff routes, not the full native-session migration comparison.
sovereignty: A positive Sovereignty finding requires established E1, E2 and E4 in the declared scope. The existing access/exit/custody record for REAPER does not establish all three minimums. The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.

applications.name: Kodi
E3: Source distinguishes per-item NFO from a dated XML/artwork export and makes reconstruction depend on available scraper add-ons; scraper settings are not exported in that route. Complete watched/resume, profile, settings/add-on and media dependency recovery remains unestablished.
E5: Library cleanup treats missing files on reachable sources differently from unavailable sources, with conditional prompts and silent retention. This concerns library records, not automatically media-byte deletion. Effective source/remove/add-on authority and correction of record/history loss remain insufficiently covered.
longevity: E3 is not established for Kodi's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.
applications.remaining: Watched/resume/artwork round-trip comparison, independent database reading, profile migration/downgrade and observed cleanup/source-removal behavior remain untested. E5 needs effective cleanup/source/removal settings, add-on authority and recoverable library/history states; record cleanup and media deletion are distinct.
applications.current_remaining: Watched/resume/artwork round-trip comparison, independent database reading, profile migration/downgrade and observed cleanup/source-removal behavior remain untested. E5 needs effective cleanup/source/removal settings, add-on authority and recoverable library/history states; record cleanup and media deletion are distinct.
applications.next: Use a synthetic profile/database/NFO/artwork/media-reference packet with expected watched/resume records; inspect it independently and obtain same-version cleanup/source/add-on authority and restoration evidence.
sovereignty: A positive Sovereignty finding requires established E1, E2 and E4 in the declared scope. The existing access/exit/custody record for Kodi does not establish all three minimums. The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.

applications.name: KOReader
E3: Sidecar location varies by adjacent, separate-tree and hashed modes, and the inspected highlight JSON export is not the whole sidecar/settings object. No complete cross-device metadata/annotation reconstruction with checksum/path changes and compatible releases is established.
E5: Sidecar loading calls Lua dofile inside error-catching, which is not sandboxing; source also defines replacement/old-backup priorities. Effective trust of imported sidecars, write/backup policy and usable recourse after metadata migration remain insufficiently established.
longevity: E3 is not established for KOReader's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.
applications.remaining: Actual cross-device/hash-mode migration, annotation-field comparisons across export formats, PDF checksum changes, release compatibility and backup restoration remain untested. E5 needs safe sidecar trust/execution policy and effective backup/write/migration correction; data inspection must not execute untrusted Lua.
applications.current_remaining: Actual cross-device/hash-mode migration, annotation-field comparisons across export formats, PDF checksum changes, release compatibility and backup restoration remain untested. E5 needs safe sidecar trust/execution policy and effective backup/write/migration correction; data inspection must not execute untrusted Lua.
applications.next: Inspect synthetic sidecars as text/data only, alongside book hashes and a location/migration manifest; obtain same-version external annotation/move/backup records without executing sidecar code.
sovereignty: A positive Sovereignty finding requires established E1, E2 and E4 in the declared scope. The existing access/exit/custody record for KOReader does not establish all three minimums. The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.

applications.name: mpv
E3: Watch-later serialization preserves selected options with path-derived filenames and conditional positions, not the full player/configuration/script state. Complete playlists, scripts, media paths and cross-version option meaning have not been restored and compared; the existing durable-state scope cannot be treated as stateless merely to skip E3.
E5: Resume loading/precedence/mtime and state-deletion branches are concrete controls. They do not establish effective script/subprocess/network authority, output/cache overwrite policy or correction across the configured playback and saved-state workflow.
longevity: E3 is not established for mpv's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.
applications.remaining: Actual playback/cross-machine restore, version-option migration, scripts/subprocess/network observation and output/cache overwrite behavior remain untested. E5 needs script/subprocess/network and output-write policy plus saved-state deletion/recovery boundaries.
applications.current_remaining: Actual playback/cross-machine restore, version-option migration, scripts/subprocess/network observation and output/cache overwrite behavior remain untested. E5 needs script/subprocess/network and output-write policy plus saved-state deletion/recovery boundaries.
applications.next: Inspect synthetic media/playlists/config/scripts/watch-later files with expected paths/options and reference behavior; seek matching external playback/resume/script/output-write observations.
E2: The former E2 Pass does not establish preservation of the declared saved-state/script/playlist workflow in an independent player. Ordinary media files remain portable, but that narrower fact does not complete the stated profile's migration.
sovereignty: A positive Sovereignty finding requires established E1, E2 and E4 in the declared scope. The existing access/exit/custody record for mpv does not establish all three minimums. The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.

applications.name: Jellyfin
E3: NFO export can carry selected state for one configured user, not every user's records. Complete version-compatible database/config/metadata/subtitle/archive reconstruction, media preservation and cross-host per-user comparison are not demonstrated.
E5: Restore has explicit server/backup-engine version guards and destructive extraction/table-replacement steps. Those code paths do not establish effective role/target approval, delete-media scope, inspectable user-state changes and available recourse across the server workflow.
longevity: E3 is not established for Jellyfin's existing essential-record scope. The previous Longevity finding is replaced by Not assessed, not a verified failure or a positive placeholder.
transparency: The positive control observations above do not yet establish whole-scope E5. The methodology requires that minimum before a positive Transparency and Control finding; the previous positive finding is therefore withdrawn to Not assessed, not changed to Does not meet.
applications.remaining: Same-version/cross-host recovery, complete archive coverage, media-byte preservation, per-user comparison, delete-media scope and observed network behavior remain untested. E5 needs restore/target and delete-media/user authority, clear destructive-state boundaries and independent recovery evidence.
applications.current_remaining: Same-version/cross-host recovery, complete archive coverage, media-byte preservation, per-user comparison, delete-media scope and observed network behavior remain untested. E5 needs restore/target and delete-media/user authority, clear destructive-state boundaries and independent recovery evidence.
applications.next: Inspect a synthetic complete server backup plus media/config manifests and expected per-user records, then obtain same-version cross-host restore and permission/delete-media observations with explicit rollback material.
sovereignty: A positive Sovereignty finding requires established E1, E2 and E4 in the declared scope. The existing access/exit/custody record for Jellyfin does not establish all three minimums. The prior positive finding is withdrawn; recorded storage and portability strengths remain facts, not a verified failure.
